report.tagline: India's biggest food delivery app, connecting hungry diners, restaurants and delivery riders.
report.simpleSummary: Zomato is an app where you pick a restaurant, order food and a rider brings it to you, usually in about 30 minutes. Restaurants pay Zomato a cut of each order, and you pay a small fee too. If you pay for Zomato Gold, you get free delivery and discounts. Zomato is owned by Eternal, which also owns Blinkit, and food delivery is its steady, profitable business.

overview.whatItDoes: Zomato started in 2008 as a restaurant menu and review site and moved into food delivery in 2015. Today it is a three-sided marketplace: diners order food, restaurants cook it, and delivery partners bring it. Its parent company was renamed Eternal in 2025. Founder Deepinder Goyal stepped down as group CEO in January 2026 and Blinkit's Albinder Dhindsa took over.
howItWorks: Restaurants list their menus on Zomato and set prices.
Diners browse, filter by cuisine, rating, price or delivery time, and order.
Zomato assigns a nearby delivery partner who picks up the food and brings it to the diner, with live tracking.
Restaurants pay Zomato a commission on each order and can pay extra for ads to appear higher.
Diners pay the food price, a platform fee, and delivery and packaging charges unless they have Gold.
Ratings from diners help other diners choose and push restaurants to keep quality up.
overview.valueProposition: For diners: food from almost any good restaurant nearby, fast, with ratings to choose well. For restaurants: lots of extra orders without opening new outlets. For riders: flexible work and daily earnings.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Search, filters, dish photos and ratings for delivery and dining.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Zomato's oldest strength; helps diners pick and keeps restaurants honest.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Shows food preparation and rider location until it reaches you.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Reduces anxiety and support calls; speed is a key reason to pick Zomato.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: A paid membership with free delivery above a minimum order and extra discounts.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Makes heavy users order more often and choose Zomato over Swiggy.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Restaurants pay to appear higher in search and on the home screen.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: High-margin revenue that boosts profit per order.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Lets restaurants manage orders, menus, prices and see sales insights.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Good tools keep restaurants on the platform and improve food prep time.

coreFeatures.feature: Feeding India and rider welfare programmes
coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Optional donation at checkout and insurance and support for riders.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Builds brand trust and helps address criticism of gig work.

businessModel.summary: Zomato makes money from three sides. Restaurants pay commissions and ad fees. Diners pay platform fees, delivery fees and Gold membership. Out of this, Zomato pays riders and covers discounts. In mid-2026 it kept about ₹5.5 of profit for every ₹100 of food sold.

revenueStreams.detail: A cut of each order, often in the range of 18-25% depending on the deal (estimate).
Restaurants pay to rank higher and appear in banners.
Platform fee per order, delivery fee for non-members, rain and long-distance fees.

businessModel.pricing: Menu prices set by restaurants. Platform fee per order has risen over time and is around ₹10 to ₹15 in big cities (changes often). Delivery fee depends on distance and Gold status. Gold plan price varies by offer. Exact current fees not fixed or fully public.
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a ₹450 order (estimate). Zomato keeps about ₹100 to ₹110 from restaurant commission, ads and customer fees, its take rate. It pays the rider about ₹50 to ₹60, spends some on discounts and support, and is left with about ₹25 (5.5% of order value, matching its ₹627 crore EBITDA on ₹11,445 crore of orders in Q2 FY27). Profit per order rises when orders are bigger, riders carry more orders per hour, and ad income grows.

howTheyGetUsers: Witty push notifications and social media that keep the brand top of mind
Cross-promotion with Blinkit and the District app
Expanding into hundreds of smaller cities
whatBringsUsersBack: Habit of ordering dinner and late-night food
Gold savings that make Zomato the default app
Trust in ratings and quick refunds for problems
growth.moat: Zomato has a three-sided network: more diners attract more restaurants, more restaurants attract more diners, and more orders keep riders busy so delivery stays fast and cheap. Its bigger order volume than Swiggy gives it more profit per order to invest. A new player would need years to match this, as many low-commission rivals have found.

competitors.name: Swiggy
competitors.positioning: Number two in food delivery, with food and Instamart in one app and Swiggy One membership.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zomato is bigger and earns about 1.8 times Swiggy's food profit; Swiggy bundles food and groceries in one app while Zomato keeps Blinkit separate.

competitors.name: Rapido and ONDC-based food apps
competitors.positioning: Low-commission or zero-commission models that charge restaurants less.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zomato has more restaurants, users and riders; rivals compete on lower restaurant costs.

competitors.name: Restaurant direct ordering (Domino's, McDonald's own apps)
competitors.positioning: Big chains with their own apps and delivery fleets.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zomato offers choice across all restaurants; chain apps offer loyalty and no platform fee.

competitors.name: Quick commerce food (Blinkit Bistro, Zepto Cafe, Swiggy Snacc)
competitors.positioning: 10-minute snacks and meals from dark kitchens.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Zomato offers full restaurant meals and choice; quick food apps win on speed for snacks.

northStar.metric: Monthly orders delivered on time and rated 4 stars or more
northStar.why: It shows that diners got good food on time, restaurants got paid orders, and riders completed trips. Good orders also lead to repeat orders and profit.

guardrailMetrics: Food delivery adjusted EBITDA margin (about 5.5% of order value) must not fall
Rider earnings per hour and safety incidents
strengths: Largest food delivery network in India with steady profits
Strong, playful brand with high recall
Owns Blinkit, giving it data, riders and cash across food and groceries
Better profit per order than Swiggy food
weaknesses: Food delivery growth (about 21%) is slower than quick commerce
Many failed experiments (Zomato Legends, 10-minute food, quick-food apps) show trouble finding new food growth
Fees and commissions draw criticism from diners and restaurants
Group focus has shifted to Blinkit after the CEO change
risks: Competition Commission and restaurant association complaints about commissions and private labels
Low-commission rivals like Rapido taking restaurants and price-sensitive users
Gig worker welfare rules raising rider costs
Quick commerce food (10-minute snacks) eating into food orders
userComplaints: Platform fee, packaging and delivery charges make the bill much higher than the menu price
Restaurant prices on Zomato higher than dine-in
Wrong or missing items with slow refunds
Customer support hard to reach beyond chatbots

improvementIdeas.idea: Show the final 'pay this much' price on every restaurant and dish card
improvementIdeas.problem: Users feel fees are hidden until checkout.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer abandoned carts and better trust.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Checkout drop-off rate and fee complaints

improvementIdeas.idea: Kitchen prep-time alerts that give restaurants a nudge when food is running late
improvementIdeas.problem: Late or cold food hurts ratings and repeat orders.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Average prep time and on-time delivery rate

improvementIdeas.idea: Budget meals tab with dishes under ₹150 including all fees
improvementIdeas.problem: Students and smaller-city users find orders too costly.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Orders per user among new and young users

improvementIdeas.idea: Restaurant 'growth score' showing how to raise orders without ads (photos, prep time, menu changes)
improvementIdeas.problem: Restaurants feel they must pay for ads to survive.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Better restaurant loyalty and better menus for diners.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Restaurant churn and organic order growth

improvementIdeas.idea: Gold savings dashboard with monthly summary
improvementIdeas.problem: Members do not see the value and may not renew.

pmLessons: Marketplaces must keep every side happy. Pushing commissions too high can drive restaurants away, which hurts diners.
Membership works when savings are clear. Gold pays for itself in a few orders, which makes users loyal.
Experiments that fail are fine if you learn fast. Zomato shut many side projects and focused on what worked.
A strong brand voice, like witty push notifications, can be a cheap growth engine.

interviewQuestions.question: Zomato's food delivery growth has slowed to about 20%. How would you speed it up?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split growth into more users, more orders per user and bigger orders. Look at smaller cities, budget meals, new occasions (breakfast, office lunch) and Gold. Pick one with a test plan.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Zomato raise its platform fee by ₹5?
interviewQuestions.hint: Estimate extra revenue per order versus drop in orders. Test in a few cities. Watch frequency, Gold sign-ups and competitor pricing.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you balance diners, restaurants and riders when designing a new feature?
interviewQuestions.hint: Name each side's goal. Score the feature's impact on each. Choose guardrails for the sides not targeted, like restaurant churn or rider pay.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star metric for Zomato food delivery?
interviewQuestions.hint: Choose something that captures value for all sides, like on-time well-rated orders. Explain why GOV alone misses quality. Break it into users, frequency, quality and supply.

interviewQuestions.question: Diners complain food arrives cold. How do you fix it?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find the cause: prep delay, rider wait, long distance or poor packaging. Use data to see which is biggest. Propose fixes for each, with metrics.

The ₹450 average order and commission range of 18-25% are estimates, not published figures.
